key_insight: VisDom adds a visible-domain constraint to sparse novel view synthesis, helping models focus on geometry that is actually observable from the input views. This reduces overfitting, floating artifacts, and inconsistent reconstructions in sparse-view settings.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the difficulty of reconstructing accurate 3D geometry and synthesizing new views from only a few input images, where NeRF- and Gaussian Splatting-based methods often overfit and silhouette consistency alone is not enough.
method: Introduces a visible-domain constraint to limit optimization to regions supported by the observed views.
Uses this constraint to reduce ambiguity in sparse-view 3D reconstruction and prevent hallucinated geometry.
Improves view synthesis quality by discouraging floating artifacts and enforcing more consistent shape recovery.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, VisDom offers a practical way to make sparse-view reconstruction more stable and reliable without requiring dense supervision. It is especially useful for 3D capture scenarios where collecting many views is expensive or impossible.
